comparator.name: Bachelor Marine Technology
comparator.sourceNotes: TU Delft's current programme pages, checked 2026-10-03, describe a three-year bachelor that develops maritime engineers through mathematics, mechanics, marine-technology courses and integrated maritime projects. The live 'What will I learn?' page supplies the exact category-level allocation of all 180 EC and links the official curriculum chart. That chart, current on the live page and dated in its file metadata to September 2024, names the courses within each category. The complete allocation is reproduced below without inventing unsupported per-course credits.
components: The official curriculum chart names Analysis 1, Analysis 2, Linear Algebra 1, Linear Algebra 2, Analysis 3, Differential Equations, Probability and Statistics, and Numerical Mathematics.

The official curriculum chart names Statics, Strength of Materials, Dynamics, Thermodynamics, Rigid-Body Dynamics, Continuum Mechanics, and Systems and Control Engineering within the mechanics progression.

The official curriculum chart names Introduction to Marine Technology, Hydrostatics, Mechanics of Marine Structures 1 and 2, Resistance, Propulsion and Drive 1 and 2, Hydromechanics, Ship Design, Complex Loads and Vibrations, Organisation of Ship Production, and Electrical Systems and Control Engineering.
The official curriculum chart identifies Integration and Skills 1, 2 and 3 as the cumulative maritime project sequence.
Genuine 30-EC minor space preserved from the official current programme breakdown and curriculum chart.
The live programme page describes a concluding team research or design assignment under the theme green and safe at sea.

exception.reason: Marine Technology is a cumulative naval-architecture and marine-engineering degree. Its compulsory spine combines analysis, linear algebra, differential equations, probability, numerical mathematics, statics, dynamics, strength of materials, thermodynamics, rigid-body and continuum mechanics, hydromechanics, hydrostatics, marine structures, resistance, propulsion and drive systems, ship design, complex loads and vibration, electrical systems and control, ship production, integrated maritime projects and a final marine research or design project. UCR offers meaningful mathematics, programming, sustainability, water-management and general design courses. It does not offer the required engineering-mechanics, hydrodynamics, naval-architecture, marine propulsion, structural, production, control and vessel-design progression or equivalent experimental and project facilities. A UCR pathway could study sustainable maritime systems from environmental, policy and quantitative perspectives, but it would not be a defensible Marine Technology comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official programme breakdown accounts for the full 180 EC: 24 EC mathematics, 36 EC mechanics, 58 EC specialist Marine Technology courses, 20 EC integrated Marine Technology projects, a 30-EC minor and a 12-EC Bachelor Final Project. The linked curriculum chart places analysis, linear algebra, statics, dynamics, strength of materials, thermodynamics and maritime foundations in year one; differential equations, statistics, numerical mathematics, advanced mechanics, control, hydromechanics, propulsion, structures and ship design in year two; and a 30-EC minor, complex loading and vibration, electrical systems and control, ship-production organisation and the final project in year three. The programme page states that each quarter combines mathematics, mechanics, maritime technology and/or a maritime project, confirming the intentionally integrated engineering progression.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide relevant quantitative foundations. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming, DISDATA312 Robotics and DISARIN311 Optimization Methods in AI add computational and systems perspectives. ENSDELT111 Building with Nature, ENSDELT211 Living with Water, ENSSUST211 Energy & Sustainability and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design address water infrastructure, energy systems, wind and sustainable engineering contexts. BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design provides general team design, fabrication and prototyping. The workbook nevertheless contains no statics-and-dynamics sequence, strength or mechanics of materials, rigid-body or continuum mechanics, engineering thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, hydrostatics for vessel design, ship hydrodynamics and resistance, naval architecture, marine propulsion and drive systems, marine structural analysis, complex loading and vibration, ship electrical systems, ship production, vessel stability and safety, or cumulative ship-design studio. DISMATH312 covers mathematical linear-system representations rather than marine control hardware and vessel dynamics; DISDATA312 covers robot kinematics and motion planning rather than ship motions or propulsion; and the sustainability courses study environmental systems rather than engineering design and certification of floating structures. UCR also lacks the target's 20-EC staged maritime project sequence and 12-EC marine-technology final project. The closest possible UCR combination therefore remains an environmental and quantitative liberal-arts pathway with the programme's defining naval-architecture and marine-engineering formation absent.
